paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the performance of two methods—ST-ES and Random—for selecting in-context examples, measured by the minADE₂₀ metric, as the number of examples varies from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Examples," is linear and ranges from 0 to 8, with tick marks at integer intervals. The y-axis, labeled "minADE₂₀ (↓)", is also linear and ranges from 21.00 to 24.00, with tick marks at 0.50 intervals; the downward arrow indicates that lower values represent better performance. The orange line with circular markers represents the Random method, which starts at approximately 24.00 when the number of examples is 0 and remains nearly constant, showing a slight decline to around 23.70 at 8 examples. The blue line with circular markers represents the ST-ES method, which begins at approximately 24.00 at 0 examples and decreases steadily to about 21.10 at 8 examples, indicating improved performance with more examples. Both lines are solid and connected by straight segments between data points.
